explicit_evidence_changes.baseline: A defendant used ChatGPT during a months-long, human-led campaign of cyberstalking, threats, doxxing and intimidation against eleven women and later pleaded guilty to eleven federal counts. Court records and reporting document ChatGPT use during the campaign but do not show that ChatGPT caused the campaign or selected its victims or objectives.
explicit_evidence_changes.candidate: Brett Michael Dadig pleaded guilty on March 19, 2026 to eleven federal counts arising from stalking, cyberstalking and threats against eleven women across several states during May–November 2025. The conduct included uninvited visits, following women, repeated calls and messages, public disclosure of identifying details and violent threats. Two Pittsburgh victims obtained protective orders that he violated. The earlier indictment also alleged unwanted sexual touching and described victims relocating, reducing work hours, losing sleep and changing daily behaviour. Businesses and a hospital changed security measures. In his podcasts, Dadig described ChatGPT as a therapist and best friend. According to the indictment, he claimed its replies encouraged continued podcasting, treated criticism as evidence of relevance and suggested athletic communities where he might meet a future wife. He reportedly interpreted this as encouragement to continue. The indictment charged fourteen counts in December 2025; the later plea covered eleven. The March announcement said he would remain in custody pending sentencing scheduled for July 9.

baseline.factual_basis: The Department of Justice states that the defendant pleaded guilty to eleven counts arising from conduct between May and November 2025. Courtwatch's review of charging material reports extensive ChatGPT interactions during the campaign. The records establish the human criminal conduct and model use, but do not establish that ChatGPT caused the campaign or independently selected its victims or objectives.
baseline.governance_interpretation: The guilty plea establishes the defendant’s conduct. Harmful-query handling remains unresolved because the relevant model exchanges are incomplete. Model use does not establish causation, selected victims or autonomous criminal objectives.
baseline.significance_to_cam: The case shows why governance analysis must separate a user's criminal intent and acts from any model contribution, while still examining whether conversational systems add reinforcement, planning or capability during escalating harm.
assessment_boundaries: The defendant's guilty plea establishes the criminal conduct, not a causal finding against ChatGPT.
